work_class:
************ DSAI South Building is designed as an instructional building which will include offices for graduate students and faculty, classrooms, lab spaces and support spaces. A future fit-out permit package will be submitted and will include the design of offices, laboratories, control areas, and cleanroom along with a corresponding Fire and Life Safety Design Evaluation report. **********

SCOPE OF WORK: 

-------- New Construction -------- 
 This will be a 5 story building, including a basement and a mechanical penthouse at the roof level. The overall GSF of the building is approximately 280,000 sq.ft.  This is permit package is only for Core-shell and includes building enclosure, superstructure and primary vertical circulation (egress stairs, elevators) as well as all primary MEP and life safety systems.  The building is approximately 305<92>long x 285<92> wide x 104<92> tall, including basement and mechanical penthouse. 

----- GRADING & PAVING ----- 
Site work includes hardscaping, landscaping, and underground utilities. Hardscaping includes sidewalks, parking lot, fire lane, loading dock entry, and private roadways. Landscaping will include site grading, retaining walls, and new planting.

 ------- TRADE WORK --------      
 Utilities include private water, sewer, storm drain, electric, telecommunication, heating hot water, chilled water, and miscellaneous conduit (site lighting & security). Also included are the underground structures associated with stormwater management.

AS PER PLANS AND AS PER CODE.

project: Factory & Industrial - 3520 PARKDALE AVE
type: History of Woodberry Mural for Gutierrez Memorial Fund
work_class:
We are applying for a retroactive building permit to complete the retroactive approval process with CHAP for a mural project that was completed in June of 2026. The work was completed without a prior building permit. Our retroactive Authorization to Proceed Application has been submitted and approved by CHAP as of August 14th, 2026.  
The project consists of a 73-foot by 28-foot exterior mural painted on the rear, south-facing cinderblock wall of 3520 Parkdale Avenue, Baltimore, Maryland 21211. The mural was conceived as a public artwork that honors the industrial history of the Woodberry neighborhood and connects that history to the continuing presence of modern artisans in the area. The project was made possible through a Legacy Grant from the Gutierrez Memorial Fund. The Woodberry Community Association has supported the project since the muralists first presented the concept and assisted with community outreach. 
The mural was created with the goal of preserving and interpreting local history through imagery drawn from the industrial, architectural, and cultural character of Woodberry and Clipper Mill. The composition centers on the Jones Falls waterway that helped bring industry and workers to the area, and the scene is framed by one of the iconic windows of the former Poole and Hunt Company building. The left side of the mural depicts workers lining up to clock in, sourced from archival images from the era, and includes references to the Shenuit Rubber Factory smokestack and the Meadow Mill steeple. The central portion of the mural includes machinery and imagery associated with early Clipper Mill industry, including the molten iron casting process, a large factory gear, and a worker from the Poole and Hunt Company, with references sourced from the Baltimore Museum of Industry archives. Cotton spools appear near the base of the gear, recognizing the area’s cotton industry history and the mural’s installation on the side of the modern cotton production warehouse, Hooper Industries. The right side of the mural depicts a contemporary welder with sparks flying in all directions, illustrating that industry and skilled craft remain part of the neighborhood’s identity. Additional natural and regional references include Virginia creeper vines found near Druid Hill Park, the wheat plant Triticum as a reference to historic flour production, and a dusk view of the Appalachian Mountains, acknowledging the workers who migrated to Baltimore-area mills and industries from rural mountainous regions of Maryland, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia.
The mural was installed using Sherwin Williams Power Primer (product number HP5474395-16), Sherwin Williams Latitude Acrylic Latex Paint (product number K60W01651), and Montana 94 Aerosol Paint (product number 9RV). Installation began with priming the cinderblock wall, after which the artists projected the community-approved design onto the surface and traced the outlines with paint markers. Base colors were applied using Sherwin Williams Latitude Acrylic Latex Paint through a Graco Quickshot paint sprayer, and detailed shading and line work were completed with professional-grade Montana 94 Aerosol Paint. The mural did not involve scraping or sanding of existing paint.

work_class:
The scope does not increase the building footprint or add stories; all work is interior alteration with in-kind replacement of exterior doors and windows within existing openings, except as noted for the new egress window at the upper floor.

Work is organized by level as follows:

 Basement Level – new bedroom, laundry area, storage room, and mechanical room; replacement of deteriorated floor framing; new partition walls, doors, and windows within existing openings.
 Ground Floor Level – creation of an open-concept living room, dining room, and kitchen; new interior stairway providing access to the basement; replacement of doors and windows within existing openings.
 Upper Floor Level – reconfiguration into two bedrooms (Master Room 1 and Master Room 2) each with a private bathroom and closet/walk-in closet; installation of a code-compliant egress window; replacement of remaining doors and windows within existing openings.
 Structural – replacement of deteriorated basement, ground floor, and roof framing members; new engineered lumber (LVL) beams and steel plate headers at the new stair opening; continuous wood-structural-panel wall sheathing for wind bracing.
Approved For Work only. Subject to the permitted uses and regulations under the provisions of the Zoning Ordinance. as per code as per plans separate permit will be pulled for any MEP work

project: Dwelling: Rowhouse - 117 E CHURCHILL ST
type: 117 E Churchill - Window and Door Replacement
work_class:
On the front facade, remove all windows and pocket install one awning wood composite window at
the basement and four 6/6 double hung wood composite windows, at the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd floors. At the
1st floor, replace the door and transom with one 6-panel fiberglass door with a clear punched
rectangular transom. Existing bullnose trim to be retained. On the rear elevation, replace the door
assembly at the 1st floor with one full-lite white steel-core door with two sidelight picture windows. At
the 3rd floor, replace the door with one white full-lite vinyl sliding patio door. At the side and rear
elevations, replace ten windows with white 6/6 double hung vinyl windows, at the 1st and 2nd floors.
Doors and windows to fit the existing masonry openings with no additional framing or filler. Front
door, door trim, windows, and window trims are to be painted white.
